question: The cell wall of spirogyra contains:
solution:
The correct answer is __**cellulose**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The cell wall of **spirogyra** contains **cellulose**.
 
• **Cellulose** is a polysaccharide consisting of a linear chain of several hundred to many thousands of β(1→4) linked D-glucose units.
 
• It is a primary structural component of green algae and plants, making up about 30% of their cell walls.
 
• Other substances like **lignin, suberin, and chitin** are found in different types of organisms or serve different functions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Spirogyra** is a genus of filamentous green algae of the order Zygnematales, named for the helical or spiral arrangement of the chloroplasts that is characteristic of the genus.
 
• It is commonly found in freshwater habitats and is known for its role in photosynthesis.
 
• Cellulose in the cell wall provides structural support and protection, maintaining the shape and rigidity of the cells.
